text: The pipeline begins with an enormous general text corpus, such as Wikipedia, to establish foundational language understanding.
This general corpus is used to train a multi-layer neural network during the general-domain language model pre-training phase.
The pre-trained model then feeds into the downstream flood tweet classification framework.
Here, the language model undergoes target task fine-tuning to adapt to the specific vocabulary and style of disaster text.
Tweet data collected from a specific flood area provides domain-specific text for language model tuning and classifier training.
A classification head is appended and fine-tuned to create the target task classification application.
The classifier accurately partitions messages into flood-related and flood-unrelated categories.
Finally, the transfer learning framework generalizes to classify incoming feeds from new flood locations with minimal labeled data.
